lesson_scope: Work-energy principle in the presence of friction and resistance forces (Work done by driving forces = change in KE + change in GPE + work done against friction/resistance); resolving forces on rough inclined planes to evaluate normal reaction and limiting friction (Fr = mu * R); speed and distance determination using energy accounting; comparative analysis of work done on multi-segment tracks and round trips.

Set up the work-energy balance for the upward journey to rest at $A$:
$$E_{k\text{,start}} = \Delta E_p + W_{\text{fric,leg}}$$
$$216 = mg(d\sin 20^\circ) + 71.25$$
$$30\sin 20^\circ d = 216 - 71.25 = 144.75\text{ J}$$

Solve for the distance $d$ travelled up the plane:
$$d = \frac{144.75}{30\sin 20^\circ} = \frac{144.75}{10.2606} \approx 14.1073\text{ m} \approx 14.1\text{ m}$$

Equate the work done against friction to $\mu R d$ to find $\mu$:
$$W_{\text{fric,leg}} = \mu (mg\cos 20^\circ) d = 71.25$$
$$\mu(30\cos 20^\circ)(14.1073) = 71.25$$
$$\mu(28.1908)(14.1073) = 71.25 \implies 397.697\mu = 71.25$$
$$\mu = \frac{71.25}{397.697} \approx 0.179159 \approx 0.179$$
Alternatively, $\mu = \tan 20^\circ \left(\frac{71.25}{144.75}\right) \approx 0.179$.

$$\Delta E_p = 216 - 71.25 = 144.75\text{ J}$$

Determine coefficient of friction:
- Comparing friction work to potential energy gain:
$$\frac{W_{\text{fric}}}{\Delta E_p} = \frac{\mu \cos 20^\circ}{\sin 20^\circ} = \frac{\mu}{\tan 20^\circ}$$
- Solving directly for $\mu$:
$$\mu = \tan 20^\circ \times \frac{71.25}{144.75} \approx 0.179$$
